title: Atlantic City, Galloway reach silver in sustainability - NewsBreak
text:
By Fideri News Network report ,
1 days ago
Atlantic City and Galloway Township are tops in the county for sustainability this year, according to awards given by Sustainable Jersey.
The group recognized 83 state municipalities that achieved Bronze and Silver certification this year before a capacity crowd in the Crown Ballroom at the Sheraton Hotel during the NJ League of Municipalities Conference.
The event celebrated the top municipalities and their accomplishments in advancing local sustainability.
To become certified, municipalities must complete a range of sustainability actions and document their progress. Bronze-level certification requires a minimum of 150 points, while silver-level certification requires 350 points or more.
Atlantic City and Galloway achieved Silver Certification with 430 points and 390 point, respectively.
Linwood, Pleasantville and Somers Point achieved Bronze Certification.
“It’s inspiring to see communities of every size across New Jersey leading the way toward a more sustainable and resilient future,” Sustainable Jersey Director Randall Solomon said. “These municipalities are not waiting for change, they’re creating it, through action, innovation, and collaboration.”
Currently, 191 towns are certified, and Sustainable Jersey’s 468 participating communities represent nearly 83% of the state’s municipalities.
See the full list of the 2025 Sustainable Jersey Certified Municipalities here.
Established in 2009, the Sustainable Jersey Annual Awards celebrate municipalities and leaders who demonstrate outstanding commitment to sustainability.
